results.title: Frontiers | Syllable-rate-adjusted-modulation (SRAM) predicts clear and conversational speech intelligibility
results.content: Try the new design now and help us make it even better Hum. Neurosci., 11 February 2024 # Syllable-rate-adjusted-modulation (SRAM) predicts clear and conversational speech intelligibility Ye Yang1\*Fan-Gang Zeng1,2\* * 1Department of Biomedical Engineering, University of California, Irvine, Irvine, CA, United States * 2Department of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery, University of California, Irvine, Irvine, CA, United States **Introduction:** Objectively predicting speech intelligibility is important in both telecommunication and human-machine interaction systems. **Methods:** We proposed a Syllable-Rate-Adjusted-Modulation (SRAM) index to predict the intelligibility of clear and conversational speech. The most important difference between the two metrics was that the SRAM removed spectrum components below the syllable rate for intelligibility prediction, whereas the speech-based STI included all components from 0.25 to 25 Hz. We also tested the utility of SRAM in predicting the clear speech advantage against three objective metrics: ER-STI, the hearing-aid speech perception index version 2 (HASPI-v2) (Kates and Arehart, 2021), and the short-time objective intelligibility (STOI) (Taal et al., 2011). Figure 3C shows the SRAM prediction using the estimated syllable rates (SRAM*est*), which produced slightly worse prediction than the SRAM but still better than the TMP, with a clear speech benefit difference of 0.8 dB for the female speaker, 0.3 dB for the male and an overall σ of 4.8%. The SRAM outperformed not only the modulation power model without the syllable rate adjustment but also three acoustic-based objective metrics and five ASR systems in terms of predicting both the speech reception thresholds and the clear speech benefits (Figures 3–5). Second, STOI used a time-window of 384 ms to calculate the correlation, which would ignore modulation frequencies below 2.6 Hz. Because the female clear speech has a syllable rate of 1 Hz, STOI did not capture the modulation power between 1 and 2.6 Hz in the clear speech, resulting in predicting prediction a clear speech disadvantage (Figure 4C left panel). The present study demonstrated that a syllable-rate-adjusted-modulation index or SRAM can predict sentence-level speech intelligibility and the intelligibility benefit of clear speech over conversational speech at the same signal-to-noise ratio. doi: 10.1044/1092-4388(2006/029) Keywords: objective metric, speech intelligibility, clear speech, temporal modulation, automatic speech recognition Citation: Yang Y and Zeng F-G (2024) Syllable-rate-adjusted-modulation (SRAM) predicts clear and conversational speech intelligibility.

German audio metering pioneer RTW announced a new Speech Intelligibility Meter, developed in cooperation with Fraunhofer IDMT. At IBC 2025, the company showcased further advanced metering solutions for immersive audio and AI-powered analysis based on is new TMxCore audio metering platform. RTW also announced a new Network Display feature for its TouchMonitor 5 and TouchControl 5 platforms, allowing users to display metering or monitoring in a standard web browser, completely independent of the device’s on-screen content. The new RTW Speech Intelligibility Meter helps broadcast and professional audio engineers identify and address issues in film, television, streaming, and live production. Whether it is unclear dialogue in a drama series, competing background music in reality TV, or crowd noise overwhelming commentators in a sports broadcast, the RTW Speech Intelligibility Meter offers an intelligent, AI-powered solution for identifying speech intelligibility challenges in any production environment. “With the Speech Intelligibility Meter, powered by Fraunhofer IDMT’s AI technology, we give broadcasters and post-production professionals an objective tool to ensure dialogue always remains clear and engaging - eliminating the guesswork from critical mixing decisions.”. This advanced metering platform, based on RTW's trusted TouchMonitor TM7/TM9 technology, combines proven measurement accuracy with powerful processing resources, and is designed to evolve and support evolving workflows in broadcast, post-production, and immersive audio. Also unveiled at IBC 2025, the new Network Display feature for RTW’s TouchMonitor 5 and TouchControl 5 platforms, allows users to display metering or monitoring in a standard web browser, completely independent of the device’s on-screen content.

results.content: Subjective Measure** : A number of studies consider either a single criterion such as overall quality , preference or musical noise salience or a set of criteria restricted to speech for subjective analysis of separated speech signals. a. Time and Frequency Signal to Noise Ratio Measures :. Spectral distance measures based on Linear Predictive Coding (LPC) are techniques used to quantify the difference between two audio signals in terms of their spectral characteristics. These measures can be useful in various applications, including audio signal processing, speech recognition, and source separation. Signal-to-distortion ratio (SDR) is a measure used to quantify the quality of a signal in comparison to its distorted or noisy version. It measures the ratio of the clean speech signal’s energy to the energy of the residual noise or interference, while being insensitive to the scaling of the signals. NB-PESQ is an extension of the Perceptual Evaluation of Speech Quality (PESQ) algorithm designed to handle signals with a narrower frequency range.

results.title: The Future of Audio Forensics: Trends, Innovations, and ...
results.content: * Basic audio analysis techniques involve peak level checks, balance evaluations between channels, phase scope measurements, waveform analyses * Advanced audio authentication techniques include acoustic fingerprinting for identifying changes or manipulations in recordings, * Immersive Audio creates a 3D sound experience using binaural recording techniques and object – based formats, * Spatial Audio simulates real – life sound perception by creating sounds from different directions, * Virtual Reality enables immersive analysis of crime scenes or evidence in an interactive environment, * AI and ML analyze recordings for anomalies,tampering alterations,and enhance speech intelligibility, * Cloud – Based Audio Production allows remote access to files for collaboration among professionals. Recognized as critical components in criminal identification through speech recognition (important fact 10), these techniques epitomize how technological advancements have revolutionized the field of audio forensics. ### Advanced audio authentication techniques In the field of audio forensics, advanced audio authentication techniques have emerged as a crucial tool for investigating cases involving audio evidence. The Future of Audio Forensics In the future, audio forensics will play a crucial role in standardizing investigative processes, overcoming evidence collection challenges, and advancing audio authentication techniques. Additionally, advancements in speech recognition technology allow for more precise identification and authentication of voices, further enhancing the accuracy and reliability of audio forensic investigations. As advancements continue to shape our technological landscape at an unprecedented pace,the field of audio engineering alongside cloud-based storage solutions backed by Dell Technologies will undoubtedly play a pivotal role in shaping the future of audio forensics itself – evolving its capabilities even further for more accurate investigation outcomes. Some current trends in audio forensics include the use of machine learning and artificial intelligence to enhance audio analysis, advancements in voice recognition technology, and the development of tools for analyzing digital audio formats. Technological advancements play a crucial role in the future of audio forensics by providing more sophisticated tools and techniques for enhancing and analyzing audio evidence. Examples include automatic speaker recognition software, which can identify speakers based on their unique voice characteristics; advanced noise reduction algorithms that enhance intelligibility; and spectral editing tools that allow forensic experts to isolate specific sounds or voices within an audio recording.
